title: Tuesday Quick Tip
subtitle: Move on before boredom
hook: How do you know when a drill has gone on too long?
intro: The drill was great for five minutes.
Now kids are sitting down in line.
statement: The best time to change a drill is just before kids get bored.
q1: Do you switch drills on a timer —
q2: or watch the kids and change when energy drops?
q3: What are the first signs a drill is done?
t1: Every team is different. But energy stays up
t2: when drills end while kids still like them.
cta: Coaches — when do you change drills?
ctaLines: Timer. Watch their faces. Add a twist.
ctaPrompt: Share your pacing habit below. There are no wrong answers.
caption:
How do you know when a drill has gone on too long?
The drill was great for five minutes. Now kids are sitting down in line.
The best time to change a drill is just before kids get bored.
Change on a timer or change on feel. There is no single right way.
When do you change drills? Share your habit in the comments.
